facts.fact_text: On 23 April 2012 five individuals (Mr I. Bakirov, Mr S. Davidis, Ms Y. Lukyanova, Ms N. Mityushkina and Mr S. Udaltsov) submitted notice of a public demonstration to the mayor of Moscow.

The aim of the demonstration notified on 23 April 2012 was to protest against abuses and falsifications in the course of the elections to the State Duma and of the President of the Russian Federation, and to demand fair elections, respect for human rights, the rule of law and the international obligations of the Russian Federation.

On 3 May 2012 the Moscow Department of Regional Security approved the route of the demonstration from Kaluzhskaya Square, down Bolshaya Yakimanka Street and Bolshaya Polyanka Street, followed by a meeting at Bolotnaya Square.
The march on 6 May 2012 began at 4.30 p.m. at Kaluzhskaya Square.
The march on 6 May 2012 went down Yakimanka Street peacefully and without disruption.
On 6 May 2012 the applicant arrived at Bolotnaya Square to take part in the demonstration.
According to the applicant, he did not take part in any disorder or clashes with the police on 6 May 2012, although he was in the area where clashes occurred.
On 6 May 2012 the applicant was arrested during the dispersal of a political rally at Bolotnaya Square in Moscow.
The applicant was found guilty of failure to obey lawful police orders, an offence under Article 19.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
The applicant was subsequently charged with participation in mass disorder, a criminal offence provided for by Article 212 § 2 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation.
The applicant was subsequently charged with having committed violent acts against police officers, a criminal offence provided for by Article 318 § 1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation.
The applicant was detained and tried on the charges of participation in mass disorder and violent acts against police officers.
The applicant was convicted to a prison term of two years and three months.

On 6 May 2012 the Investigative Committee of the Russian Federation opened a criminal investigation into the suspected mass disorder and violent acts against the police under Articles 212 § 2 and 318 § 1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation.
On 28 May 2012 an investigation was launched into the criminal offence of organising mass disorder under Article 212 § 1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation.
On 28 May 2012 the two criminal cases — into mass disorder and violent acts against the police, and into organising mass disorder — were joined.

The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow found eight individuals, including the applicant, guilty of participation in mass disorder and of violent acts against police officers during the public assembly on 6 May 2012.
The applicant was sentenced to two years and six months' imprisonment by the Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow in the first Bolotnaya case judgment of 21 February 2014.
The first Bolotnaya case judgment of 21 February 2014 was upheld by the Moscow City Court on 20 June 2014.
The Moscow City Court on 20 June 2014 reduced the applicant's prison sentence from two years and six months to two years and three months.
The applicant was arrested shortly after throwing the small round yellow object on 6 May 2012.
On 17 May 2012 the applicant was charged with non-compliance with a lawful order by a police officer on 6 May 2012.
The applicant was found guilty of the offence provided by Article 19.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences and was sentenced to 24-hours' detention.
On 18 June 2012 charges were brought against the applicant under Article 212 § 2 (participation in mass disorder) of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation.
On 18 June 2012 charges were brought against the applicant under Article 318 § 1 (violence against a public official) of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation.
On 21 February 2014 the Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow pronounced judgment in the applicant's criminal case.

The applicant was sentenced to two years and six months' imprisonment by the Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow on 21 February 2014, calculated on the basis of a two-year prison term under Article 212 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation partly concurrent with a one-year prison term under Article 318 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation.
The applicant appealed against the first-instance judgment of 21 February 2014.
On 20 June 2014 the Moscow City Court upheld the first-instance judgment of 21 February 2014.

On 20 June 2014 the Moscow City Court reduced the applicant's prison sentence to two years and three months, comprising a one-year-and-nine-month term under Article 212 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation and a nine-month term under Article 318 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation, to run partly concurrently.
On 8 September 2014 the applicant was released after serving his prison term.

Article 212 § 1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation provides that the organisation of mass disorder accompanied by violence, riots, arson, destruction of property, use of firearms, explosives and explosive devices, as well as armed resistance to a public official, shall be punishable by four to ten years' deprivation of liberty.

Article 212 § 2 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation provides that participation in the types of mass disorder provided for by Article 212 § 1 shall be punishable by three to eight years' deprivation of liberty.

Article 212 § 3 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation provides that the instigation of mass disorder provided for by Article 212 § 1, or the instigation of participation in it, or the instigation of violence against citizens, shall be punishable by restriction of liberty for up to two years, or community works for up to two years, or deprivation of liberty for the same term.

Article 318 § 1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation provides that the use of violence not endangering life or health, or the threat to use such violence against a public official or his relatives in connection with the performance of his or her duties, shall be punishable by a fine of up to 200,000 roubles or an equivalent of the convicted person's wages for 18 months, or community works for up to five years, or up to five years' deprivation of liberty.
On 5 May 2012 the Police Chief of the Moscow Department of the Interior adopted a plan for safeguarding public order in Moscow on 6 May 2012 (the security plan).

The security plan provided for security measures in Moscow city centre in view of the forthcoming authorised demonstration at Bolotnaya Square and anticipated attempts by other opposition groups to hold unauthorised public gatherings.
The security plan set up operational headquarters to implement the security measures.

On 6 May 2012 the Investigative Committee of the Russian Federation opened a criminal investigation into the suspected mass disorder and violent acts against the police under Articles 212 § 2 and 318 § 1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation.

The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court found that between 4 p.m. and 8 p.m. on 6 May 2012 at Bolotnaya Square, unidentified persons called those present to move outside the agreed meeting venue, to defy the lawful orders of the police, and to use violence, which led to mass disorder accompanied by the use of violence against public officials and the destruction of property.

The background facts relating to the planning, conduct and dispersal of the assembly at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012 are set out in more detail in the judgment Frumkin v. Russia (no. 74568/12, §§ 7-65, 5 January 2016).
The Moscow Department of Regional Security noted on 3 May 2012 that the organisers had provided a detailed plan of the proposed events.
The march approved on 3 May 2012 was to begin at 4 p.m.
The meeting approved on 3 May 2012 had to finish by 7.30 p.m.
The number of participants for the demonstration approved on 3 May 2012 was indicated as 5,000.
On 4 May 2012 the First Deputy Head of the Moscow Department of Regional Security held a working meeting with the organisers of the demonstration at Bolotnaya Square to discuss security issues.

At the working meeting on 4 May 2012, the organisers and the authorities agreed that the assembly layout and the security arrangements would be identical to the previous public event organised by the same group of opposition activists on 4 February 2012.
At the public event on 4 February 2012, the venue of the meeting had included the park at Bolotnaya Square and the Bolotnaya embankment.

On 5 May 2012 the Tsentralnyy District Prosecutor's Office of Moscow issued a warning to Mr S. Davidis against exceeding the notified number of participants and against erecting camping tents at the meeting venue.

On 5 May 2012 the Tsentralnyy District Prosecutor's Office of Moscow issued a warning to Mr S. Udaltsov against exceeding the notified number of participants and against erecting camping tents at the meeting venue.
The intention to erect camping tents at the meeting venue was allegedly expressed by the organisers at the working meeting on 4 May 2012.
On 5 May 2012 the Moscow Department of the Interior published on its website official information about the forthcoming demonstration on 6 May 2012, including a map.
The map published by the Moscow Department of the Interior on 5 May 2012 indicated the route of the march, the traffic restrictions and an access plan to Bolotnaya Square.
The map published by the Moscow Department of the Interior on 5 May 2012 delineated the area allotted to the meeting, which included the park at Bolotnaya Square.
The map published by the Moscow Department of the Interior on 5 May 2012 marked access to the meeting through the park at Bolotnaya Square.
The police units assigned to police the march and the meeting on 6 May 2012 counted 2,400 riot police officers, of which 1,158 were on duty at Bolotnaya Square.
The police officers assigned to the demonstration on 6 May 2012 were instructed to search the demonstrators to prevent them from taking tents to the site of the meeting.
The police officers assigned to the demonstration on 6 May 2012 were instructed to obstruct access to Bolshoy Kamenyy bridge, diverting the marchers to Bolotnaya embankment, the place of the meeting.
The security plan required that the adjacent park at Bolotnaya Square be cordoned off.
At about 1.30 p.m. on 6 May 2012 the organisers were allowed access to the meeting venue to set up their stage and sound equipment.
On 6 May 2012 the police searched the vehicles delivering the stage and sound equipment and seized three tents found amid the gear.
On 6 May 2012 the police arrested several people for bringing tents to the meeting venue.
At the beginning of the march on 6 May 2012, the organisers signed an undertaking to ensure public order during the demonstration.

At the beginning of the march on 6 May 2012, the organisers gave assurances to the police that the limits on the place and time allocated for the assembly would be respected and that no tents would be placed on Bolotnaya Square.
The turnout at the march on 6 May 2012 exceeded expectations, but there is no consensus as to the exact numbers.
The official estimate of participants at the march on 6 May 2012 was 8,000.
The organisers considered that there were about 25,000 participants at the march on 6 May 2012.
The media reported different numbers of participants at the march on 6 May 2012, some significantly exceeding the official and organisers' estimates.
At about 5 p.m. on 6 May 2012 the march approached Bolotnaya Square.
The leaders of the march found that the layout of the meeting and the placement of the police cordon at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012 did not correspond to what they had anticipated.
Unlike on 4 February 2012, the park at Bolotnaya Square was excluded from the meeting venue on 6 May 2012, which was limited to Bolotnaya embankment.

Faced with the police cordon and unable to access the park at Bolotnaya Square, the leaders of the march — Mr S. Udaltsov, Mr A. Navalnyy, Mr B. Nemtsov and Mr I. Yashin — stopped and demanded that the police open access to the park.
The cordon officers at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012 did not enter into any discussion with the protest leaders.
No senior police officer was delegated to negotiate with the protest leaders at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012.

At 5.16 p.m. on 6 May 2012, after about fifteen minutes of attempting to engage with the cordon officers, Mr S. Udaltsov, Mr A. Navalnyy, Mr B. Nemtsov and Mr I. Yashin announced that they were going on a sit-down strike and sat on the ground.
After the four leaders sat down at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012, the people behind them stopped, although some people continued to go past them towards the stage.

Between 5.20 p.m. and 5.45 p.m. on 6 May 2012 two State Duma deputies tried to negotiate the enlargement of the restricted area at Bolotnaya Square by moving the police cordon behind the park along the lines expected by the organisers.

Between 5.20 p.m. and 5.45 p.m. on 6 May 2012 the Ombudsman of the Russian Federation, at the request of police, attempted to persuade the leaders of the sit-in to resume the procession and to head towards the meeting venue at Bolotnaya embankment where the stage had been set up.
During the period between 5.20 p.m. and 5.45 p.m. on 6 May 2012, no senior police officer or municipal official came to the site of the sit-down protest at Bolotnaya Square.
During the period between 5.20 p.m. and 5.45 p.m. on 6 May 2012, there was no direct communication between the authorities and the leaders of the sit-in at Bolotnaya Square.
At 5.50 p.m. on 6 May 2012 the crowd around the sit-down protest at Bolotnaya Square built up, causing some congestion.
At 5.50 p.m. on 6 May 2012 the leaders abandoned the sit-down protest and headed towards the stage, followed by the crowd.

At 5.55 p.m. on 6 May 2012 the media reported that the police authorities were regarding the sit-down strike at Bolotnaya Square as a provocation of mass disorder and were considering prosecuting those responsible for it.

At approximately 5.55 p.m. on 6 May 2012 a commotion near the police cordon occurred at the place vacated by the sit-down protest at Bolotnaya Square, and the police cordon was broken in several places.
A crowd of about 100 people spilled over into the empty space beyond the police cordon at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012.
Within seconds of the cordon being broken at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012, the police restored the cordon, which was reinforced by an additional riot police force.
Those who found themselves outside the police cordon at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012 wandered around, uncertain what to do next.

Several people were apprehended at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012 after the cordon was broken, others were pushed back inside the cordon, and some continued to loiter outside or walked towards the park.
The police cordon at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012 began to push the crowd into the restricted area and advanced by several metres, pressing it inwards.
At 6 p.m. on 6 May 2012 Ms Mityushkina, on police instructions, announced from the stage that the meeting was now over.
Ms Mityushkina's announcement at 6 p.m. on 6 May 2012 that the meeting was over was apparently not heard by most of the demonstrators or the media reporters broadcasting from the spot.
The live television footage provided by the parties at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012 contained no mention of Ms Mityushkina's announcement that the meeting was over.
At approximately 6 p.m. on 6 May 2012 a Molotov cocktail was launched from the crowd at the corner of Malyy Kamennyy bridge over the restored police cordon at Bolotnaya Square.
The Molotov cocktail launched at the corner of Malyy Kamennyy bridge on 6 May 2012 landed outside the cordon and a passer-by's trousers caught fire.
The fire caused by the Molotov cocktail at Malyy Kamennyy bridge on 6 May 2012 was promptly extinguished by the police.
At 6.15 p.m. on 6 May 2012 at the corner of Malyy Kamennyy bridge the riot police began breaking into the demonstration to split up the crowd.

Running in tight formations at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012, the riot police pushed the crowd apart, arrested some people, confronted others, and formed new cordons to isolate sections of the crowd.

Some protesters at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012 held up metal barriers and aligned them so as to resist the police, threw various objects at the police, shouted and chanted 'Shame!' and other slogans.
Whenever the police apprehended someone from among the protesters at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012, other protesters attempted to pull them back.
The police at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012 applied combat techniques and used truncheons.
At 6.20 p.m. on 6 May 2012 Mr S. Udaltsov climbed onto the stage at the opposite end of Bolotnaya Square to address the meeting and was arrested.
At approximately 6.20 p.m. on 6 May 2012 Mr A. Navalnyy attempted to go up onto the stage at Bolotnaya Square but was arrested.
At approximately 6.25 p.m. on 6 May 2012 Mr B. Nemtsov was arrested at Bolotnaya Square.

At Malyy Kamennyy bridge on 6 May 2012 the police continued dividing the crowd and began pushing some sections away from the venue, asking participants through loudspeakers to leave for the metro station.
The dispersal of the demonstration at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012 continued for at least another hour after 6.20 p.m. until the venue was fully cleared of all protesters.

At one point during the dispersal of the demonstration on 6 May 2012, the applicant picked up from the ground a small round yellow object and threw it over the heads of the protesters in the direction of the police.
The applicant was accused of shouting slogans during the events of 6 May 2012 at Bolotnaya Square.
The applicant was accused of throwing an unidentified small round yellow object that hit police officer F.'s shoulder during the events of 6 May 2012 at Bolotnaya Square.

The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court found that between 4 p.m. and 8 p.m. on 6 May 2012 at Bolotnaya Square, unidentified persons called those present to move outside the agreed meeting venue, to defy the lawful orders of the police, and to use violence, which led to mass disorder accompanied by the use of violence against public officials and the destruction of property.
The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court found that at 5 p.m. at the latest on 6 May 2012 the defendants acquired the criminal intent to participate in mass disorder and to use violence.

The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court found that the applicant (Mr Belousov) acquired an unidentified solid yellow round object at an unidentified time and place with the intention of using it to cause violence against officials.
The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court found that the applicant (Mr Belousov) repeatedly chanted anti-government slogans together with other participants in the mass disorder.
The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court found that participants in the mass disorder threw chunks of tarmac, stones, sticks and other objects at the police, hitting them on various body parts.
The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court found that the applicant (Mr Belousov) used violence not endangering the life or health of police officer F.

The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court found that between 5 p.m. and 8.10 p.m. on 6 May 2012 unidentified participants in the mass disorder deliberately administered at least three blows and kicks to police officer F.'s head, body and limbs, after which the applicant (Mr Belousov) deliberately threw an unidentified solid yellow round object which hit police officer F. on the upper right side of the chest, causing him physical pain.

The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court found that as a result of the applicant's (Mr Belousov's) and other unidentified persons' actions, police officer F. sustained physical pain and injuries in the form of bruising and abrasion of the soft tissues of the parietal region, bruising of the left forearm, and abrasion on the right shin, which constituted injuries not endangering life or health and not entailing short-term health impairment or minor durable professional incapacitation.

The applicant (Mr Belousov) pleaded not guilty at trial and testified that he went to Malyy Kamennyy Bridge to see why the meeting was not starting, saw the riot police cordon and officers arresting some participants, was looking to leave, went to the middle of Bolotnaya Square, saw a girl who tripped on something and nearly fell, picked up an object from the ground that felt soft and slimy, threw it away without aiming it at anyone, joined hands with other protesters chanting slogans, and was then grabbed by three police officers and carried to the police vehicle.

Police officer F. testified at trial that after the cordon was restored he was heading into the crowd to arrest offenders, somebody hit him three times on the head, then he felt a blow from a heavy object on his shoulder, and from the corner of his eye he saw the applicant (Mr Belousov) take a swing and toss something like a billiard ball.
The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court found that the applicant (Mr Belousov) was filmed at the moment he threw a yellow object at the police.

The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court rejected the defendants' argument that no mass disorder took place, finding that premeditated actions of a group of individuals who organised obstruction to the demonstrators' march caused discontent among the protesters towards the police, and that those leading the march changed their tactics and called for a sit-in, hoping to secure a change in the placement of the cordon; as a result, protesters forced their way through the police cordon and public order was disrupted.

The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court took into account the nature and degree of the applicant's involvement in the mass disorder and considered it possible to give him a sentence below the minimum punishment provided for by Article 212 § 2 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation.

The applicant was sentenced to two years and six months' imprisonment by the Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow on 21 February 2014, calculated on the basis of a two-year prison term under Article 212 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation partly concurrent with a one-year prison term under Article 318 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation.

In his appeal, the applicant contested the first-instance court's finding that mass disorder had taken place, alleging that there had only been isolated clashes between the protesters and the police, caused by the authorities' last-minute decision to alter the layout of the meeting venue and aggravated by their excessive crowd-control measures.
In his appeal, the applicant denied that the object he threw hit anybody.

In his appeal, the applicant alleged a breach of procedure for questioning in confrontation with the victim, police officer F., and complained that the court had refused to have the records of police officer F.'s interrogation conducted during the investigation read out.
On 20 June 2014 the Moscow City Court upheld the first-instance judgment of 21 February 2014.

On 20 June 2014 the Moscow City Court reduced the applicant's prison sentence to two years and three months, comprising a one-year-and-nine-month term under Article 212 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation and a nine-month term under Article 318 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation, to run partly concurrently.
On 8 September 2014 the applicant was released after serving his prison term.
